title: Coefficient program resource bounds
statement: Let a deterministic Goldreich–Levin input have dimension $n>0$, rational accuracy $a/b$ with $a>0$ and $2a\le b$, and Fourier bound $B\ge1$. For any Boolean target on $n$ sign-valued coordinates and any finite family of coordinate subsets whose size is at most the input's active cap, the coefficient program makes zero random-example calls, makes exactly the associated sample count of membership queries, and uses work at most its coefficient work budget.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the accuracy numerator is at most its denominator
Fourier bound is at least one
Target is a Boolean function on the input dimension
Family is a finite set of coordinate subsets
Family size is at most the active cap
